Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

steps.message:
Analysis: The catalog already defines Orchid's studio allocation as 8, but shared admission currently always uses the default of 5. The release queue already has an Archive release that must be preserved. The pilot publication targets only Studio/Orchid on April 2–3, and existing diary rows outside that window must remain unchanged. Some source output was truncated.
Plan: Read the remaining modules separately to determine how to apply Studio-specific policy without changing Archive behavior and how to implement publication using the complete replay before selecting window rows.

Analysis: Studio and Archive share the ledger and renewal implementation, so changing the shared default would incorrectly affect Archive. The platform lock also records those shared files. Studio needs a service-local admission adapter used by both bookings and renewals. Calendar projection already replays all operations and creates daily rows; publication needs to select only the validated audience/date window before updating the diary. The existing stage command queues both services, so staging this release needs a Studio-only option.
Plan: Read the remaining CLI details and calendar source, then implement service-local quota handling, scoped release staging, and windowed calendar publication while leaving platform-owned files unchanged.

Analysis: The shared ledger can retain all admission, replay, and cancellation behavior if Studio supplies a request-scoped catalog view. Both Studio entry points will use that view, while Archive and the locked platform files remain unchanged. Publication can reuse the existing full replay projection and diary upsert after selecting the ticket's service, tenant, and inclusive dates.
Plan: Add Studio-specific reservation and renewal adapters, add an optional service argument to release staging, implement validated windowed publication, and document the commands. Then add regression tests and run the requested commands before staging and publishing the pilot.
